problems.title: Find the missing 20 percent
problems.question: Theona answers 116 questions correctly and earns 80%. How many questions did she not answer correctly?
problems.idea: First find the total number of questions.
steps: The number not answered correctly is $145-116=29$. Check: $29/145=0.20=20\%$.

problems.title: Update an average
problems.question: Eight numbers have average 6. Add the numbers 11 and 9. Find the average of all ten numbers.
problems.idea: An average is a total divided by a count; combine totals before dividing.
steps: The first eight numbers have sum $8\cdot6=48$.
There are now 10 numbers, so the average is $68/10=6.8$.

problems.title: Measure a price reduction against the original price
problems.question: A computer drops in price from 1,200 GEL to 900 GEL. Find the percentage decrease.
problems.idea: Use the original price as the base of the percentage.
steps: The fraction of the original price removed is $300/1200=1/4$.

problems.title: Share a profit proportionally
problems.question: Distribute a 24,000 GEL profit in proportion to investments of 15,000 GEL by Dato, 12,000 GEL by Mariam, and 9,000 GEL by Lasha.
problems.idea: Each investor receives the same fraction of profit as their fraction of the total investment.
steps: Mariam receives $24000\cdot12000/36000=8000$ GEL; Lasha receives $24000\cdot9000/36000=6000$ GEL.
Check: the shares add to 24,000 GEL and are in the ratio $10000:8000:6000=5:4:3$, the same as the investments.
problems.answer: Dato: 10,000 GEL; Mariam: 8,000 GEL; Lasha: 6,000 GEL.

problems.title: Combine successive percentage changes
problems.question: A suit rises in price by 10%, then falls by 15%. By what percentage is its final price lower than its original price?
problems.idea: The second percentage applies to the increased price, so multiply price factors.
steps: Let the original price be $P$. After the increase it is $1.10P$.
The decrease relative to the original is $P-0.935P=0.065P$, or $6.5\%$.
For example, 100 GEL becomes 110 GEL and then 93.50 GEL.

problems.title: Dilute a solution without changing the solute
problems.question: A 15% solution becomes 12% after one glass of water is added. Find the concentration after a second identical glass of water is added.
problems.idea: Adding pure water changes the total amount, but leaves the dissolved substance unchanged.
formulas: For dilution, $c_1V_1=c_2V_2$ when the percentages use the same amount measure.
steps: Let the initial amount be $V$ and one glass be $g$. The unchanged solute gives $0.15V=0.12(V+g)$.
The solute amount is $0.15\cdot4g=0.6g$. After two glasses, the total amount is $4g+2g=6g$.

problems.title: Split a straight angle
problems.question: An angle is $7/3$ of its adjacent supplementary angle. Find it.
problems.idea: Adjacent supplementary angles add to 180 degrees.
steps: Write the required angle as $7t$ and the adjacent angle as $3t$.
The required angle is $7\cdot18^\circ=126^\circ$. The other is $54^\circ$, and $126/54=7/3$.

problems.title: Undo an angle bisector
problems.question: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. A bisector of one resulting angle makes $40^\circ$ angles with the parallel lines. Find the resulting intersection angles.
problems.idea: A bisector halves an angle, and angles on a straight line are supplementary.
formulas: $\text{adjacent angles sum to }180^\circ$; corresponding and vertically opposite angles are equal.
steps: Vertical angles give the same two values at that intersection. Parallel-line angle equalities repeat them at the other intersection.

problems.title: Put ratio points on one number line
problems.question: C divides AB in the ratio 3:7 measured from A. D divides it in the ratio 7:8 measured from B. If CD = 14 cm, find AB.
problems.idea: Use A as a common origin, taking special care with the ratio stated from B.
formulas: Distance between coordinates is the absolute difference.
steps: D lies farther from A than C. Thus $CD=AD-AC=(\frac8{15}-\frac3{10})L=\frac7{30}L$.

problems.title: Use the angle at the incenter
problems.question: The bisectors of angles A and B of triangle ABC meet at M. Angle B is half of angle AMC. Find angle B.
problems.idea: The intersection of two internal angle bisectors is the incenter, so CM also bisects angle C.
steps: Let $B=x$. The given condition is $x=\frac12\angle AMC$.
Check: $\angle AMC=90^\circ+30^\circ=120^\circ$, and half of it is $60^\circ$.
